name: Beneath the Ashes
subtitle: Where fire was meant to warm, not consume
theme: Loss / Resolve / The cost of inaction
location: Crystal Cavern to Kingdom of Ashveil

shard.name: Seal Fragment of Fire
shard.description: A smoldering red-orange crystal that burns without fuel. A fire that remembers what it used to protect.

scenes.narration: The path from the Sacred Ruins leads north — through old roads and broken bridges — until the horizon turns orange. Not dawn. The smoke reaches them first, then the heat, then the silence where a city used to be.
The Kingdom of Ashveil was once the jewel of Aethoria. Now it is a canvas of smoke and silence. Buildings that stood for centuries are rubble.
Lulu kneels beside the remains of a public garden — flowers reduced to ash, a fountain cracked and dry.

dialogue.speaker: Lulu
dialogue.text: There were people here. Families. There is a child's shoe by that wall.

dialogue.speaker: Tao
dialogue.text: ...There is no one left to guide them across. That bothers me more than it should.

dialogue.speaker: Aya
dialogue.text: This is what happens when darkness is left unopposed. I have seen what fear-driven choices cost people.

scenes.narration: An old keeper, burned and barely standing, watches them with hollow eyes.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Old Keeper: You are not shadow-soldiers. You are real. I have not seen that in weeks.

dialogue.speaker: Rei
dialogue.text: The demon lord who did this — where is he?

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Old Keeper: He was in the throne room. But he moves. He knows when something is coming. He has been waiting for something to be worth facing.

dialogue.speaker: Lulu
dialogue.text: Has anyone tried to stop him? Has anyone come?

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Old Keeper: Two did. A summoner and a winged warrior — radiant things, not from here. They fought him in the undercroft before the city fell. He did not kill them. He kept them. Said their power was too rare to waste.

dialogue.speaker: Rei
dialogue.text: He has prisoners.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Old Keeper: Chained in the deep vault beneath the palace. He feeds on their resonance to hold the Fragment steady. Without them, it would burn him alive.

dialogue.speaker: Tao
dialogue.text: So he is not just a conqueror. He is a collector. That is significantly worse.

dialogue.speaker: Aya
dialogue.text: Then we go through the cinder passage. If he is hunting us, we make him come to us on ground we choose — and we free whoever he is holding.

chapters.title: The Azure Entrance

pre_dialogue.speaker: narrator
pre_dialogue.text: The old cinder passage runs beneath the city, carved when Ashveil was young. The entrance is choked with crystalline growth.

pre_dialogue.speaker: Aya
pre_dialogue.text: The heat is rising already. Stay focused.

chapters.map_hint: Navigate Floor 1 — Find the descent to the Resonant Depths.

post_dialogue.speaker: Tao
post_dialogue.text: The air is vibrating. We are getting closer to the core.

chapters.title: The Resonant Depths

pre_dialogue.speaker: Lulu
pre_dialogue.text: The resonance is stronger here. It feels like the cavern itself is watching us.

chapters.map_hint: Navigate Floor 2 — Find the stairs to the Frozen Core.

post_dialogue.speaker: Rei
post_dialogue.text: I feel a presence below. Something ancient. Not the Demon Lord.

chapters.title: The Frozen Core

pre_dialogue.speaker: narrator
pre_dialogue.text: The heart of the cavern is a tomb of ice and crystal. The relay hums with stolen power.

chapters.map_hint: Navigate Floor 3 — Confront the Spectral Guardian and find the way into Ashveil's Undercroft.

post_dialogue.speaker: narrator
post_dialogue.text: The Spectral Guardian shatters, its resonance returning to the cavern. The path to the palace undercroft is open.

pre_dialogue.speaker: narrator
pre_dialogue.text: The Demon Lord fills the undercroft — the fire Seal Fragment blazing against his chest, the heat warping the air around him. He did not wait in his throne room. He hunted them into the tunnel and let them walk straight to him.

pre_dialogue.speaker: narrator
pre_dialogue.text: Demon Lord: You are smaller than I expected. The Fragment told me you were coming days ago. I have been patient.

pre_dialogue.speaker: narrator
pre_dialogue.text: Demon Lord: Everything that burns speaks to me. And you four burn very brightly.

pre_dialogue.speaker: Tao
pre_dialogue.text: Release them. The ones you took. A summoner and a warrior. Release them.

pre_dialogue.speaker: narrator
pre_dialogue.text: Demon Lord: My guests? They sustain the Fragment. Without their resonance anchoring it, it would have consumed me months ago. They are... useful. As you will be, once I am done with you.

pre_dialogue.speaker: Lulu
pre_dialogue.text: They are not yours to use. That Fragment does not belong to you. None of this does.

pre_dialogue.speaker: Rei
pre_dialogue.text: We have faced worse. Much worse. This ends now.

post_dialogue.speaker: narrator
post_dialogue.text: The Demon Lord falls. Not with a roar — with a sound like an exhale. Like something holding its breath for a very long time finally letting go.

post_dialogue.speaker: narrator
post_dialogue.text: The red crystal floats free from the ash. Its burning light shifts — from predatory to something older. Warmer. Like a hearthfire that remembers what homes felt like.

post_dialogue.speaker: Lulu
post_dialogue.text: It is changing. The moment he lost hold of it — it changed completely.

post_dialogue.speaker: Aya
post_dialogue.text: The corruption was in the wielder, not the Fragment itself. It was never evil. Just captured.

post_dialogue.speaker: Tao
post_dialogue.text: Two down. Three to go. I think I am starting to genuinely enjoy this quest.

post_dialogue.speaker: Rei
post_dialogue.text: You are not taking it seriously enough.

post_dialogue.speaker: Tao
post_dialogue.text: I am taking it seriously AND enjoying it. Multitasking is a core funeral director skill.

post_dialogue.speaker: narrator
post_dialogue.text: Then a presence settles over the undercroft. Not a sound. Not a figure. A weight — the kind that has no temperature, that presses from every direction at once.

post_dialogue.speaker: narrator
post_dialogue.text: Valdris: You freed the Fragment. Good. That creature was wasting it.

post_dialogue.speaker: Aya
post_dialogue.text: You are watching us.

post_dialogue.speaker: narrator
post_dialogue.text: Valdris: I have always been watching. You are the most interesting thing to enter my world in a century. The Oracle chose well — four resonances, cleanly matched. I almost respect it.

post_dialogue.speaker: Rei
post_dialogue.text: The kingdom. The people. This destruction — this is your doing. Not the Demon Lord's. Yours.

post_dialogue.speaker: narrator
post_dialogue.text: Valdris: I broke a Seal. The unraveling was a consequence. I do not govern consequences. That is what mortality is — an endless chain of consequences that someone else pays.

post_dialogue.speaker: Tao
post_dialogue.text: There was a child's shoe in that garden.

post_dialogue.speaker: narrator
post_dialogue.text: Valdris: I have consumed worlds older than that child's entire civilization. Grief is a luxury I shed six centuries ago. Come. Shatter my anchors. Break everything I have built. I will be patient.

post_dialogue.speaker: narrator
post_dialogue.text: Valdris: I am very good at patient.

post_dialogue.speaker: narrator
post_dialogue.text: The presence lifts. The ash settles. The four stand in the silence of a kingdom that will never fully recover — and carry the second Fragment forward anyway.

post_dialogue.speaker: Lulu
post_dialogue.text: He is not afraid of us at all.

post_dialogue.speaker: Rei
post_dialogue.text: No.

post_dialogue.speaker: Tao
post_dialogue.text: Good thing we are not doing this to frighten him.

post_dialogue.speaker: Aya
post_dialogue.text: Forward. That is all there is now.

dialogue.text: The deep vault beneath the undercroft shudders. Then cracks. Chains of shadow-iron, laced with the Demon Lord's binding sigils, fracture all at once — his power gone, his hold over them dissolved.

Purple light floods upward through the broken stone. From the ruins of the vault, a young woman rises — summoning robes torn at the edges, eyes blazing with the fury of creatures that have been caged too long.

dialogue.speaker: Ria
dialogue.text: My eidolons... I could hear them calling the entire time. He kept them just out of reach.

dialogue.speaker: Tao
dialogue.text: How long were you down there?

dialogue.speaker: Ria
dialogue.text: Long enough to know exactly what this Fragment has been used for. Long enough to understand what Valdris is building toward.

dialogue.speaker: Aya
dialogue.text: You are free now. And if you are willing — we still have four more Seals to break.

dialogue.speaker: Ria
dialogue.text: I am called Ria. A summoner — or I was, before all of this. I do not leave debts unpaid. I will see this through with you.
Gold and silver light tears through the vault ceiling — a winged warrior descends, armor cracked but unyielding, wings cutting ash aside as she lands with the weight of judgment made physical.

dialogue.speaker: Valka
dialogue.text: He was not strong enough to break me. Only to hold me. There is a difference.

dialogue.speaker: Rei
dialogue.text: You held for months under a binding designed to break resonance. I have guarded my own world for two thousand years. I recognize endurance when I see it.

dialogue.speaker: Valka
dialogue.text: They called me Valka, where I come from. A judge of souls. I do not remember what I was before that — only what I must do now. Valdris will be judged. When the time comes.

dialogue.speaker: Lulu
dialogue.text: Four became six. And they are not broken. They are furious. Something tells me that matters.
